thread:
alex: quick heads-up — ran an nsys capture inside the perf sandbox pod and it failed with write errors when the runtime touched the KV cache files. dumping notes here.
marie: what error did you see? nvtoolkit/file perms again?
alex: 
```
ERROR: cannot open file /var/lib/redwood/runtime/kv_cache/slot_12.kv: Permission denied
nsys: failed to write timeline output
```
sam: is the pod using hostPath with a readOnly mount? or are we running as non-root inside the container?
alex: hostPath, rw. container runs as runc rootless user (1000). dir on host is root:root with 700 — runtime assumed it could create files.
julie: this sounds like the same class of problem we saw when attaching nsight inside the runtime container — tools need special capabilities and sometimes privileged mount flags.
alex: confirmed: when I reran the pod with securityContext.privileged=true and CAP_SYS_ADMIN the capture completed and KV cache writes succeeded.
marie: privileged for prod is not acceptable. any narrower options? maybe tweak mount options or grant specific capabilities.
sam: for nvidia-container-toolkit and nsight you usually need either privileged or CAP_SYS_ADMIN + SYS_PTRACE depending on trace method. for file IO to hostPath, check fsGroup + gid/uid mapping in the podSecurityContext.
alex: tried fsGroup:1000 and uid mapping -> container process uid 1000 could write, but nsys still failed earlier during GPU kernel timeline write — looks like nsight needs permission to create temp shared memory on /dev/shm or write mmap-ed staging files.
julie: could we do an init container that chowns the host dir to the runtime uid? less blast radius than privileged.
marie: also check nvidia toolkit daemonset mounts: is /var/run/nvidia mounted with correct permissions? nsight tries to talk to the driver through that socket.
alex: logs:
```
2026-03-12T11:04:02Z runtime[pid=2154]: kvcache: failed write slot_12 -> EACCES
2026-03-12T11:04:03Z nsys: can't open staging file /tmp/nsys-XXXX: Permission denied
```
sam: another gotcha — when we run with user namespaces (rootless), hostPath ownership doesn't translate unless we use fsGroup or setgid bit. init container chown works but may hit race with multi-replica pods.
julie: for CI profiling we can spin up a special k8s profile job that runs with a tighter set of added capabilities: add CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_NICE, and mount /sys/kernel/debug as ro. then we can capture kernel timelines and nvtx markers without fully privileged.
alex: good plan. also noticed weird KV cache behavior in the trace: when a kernel fallback happened (gemm->gemm_fallback) we saw synchronous disk writes spike and stall batching. maybe our fallback path writes metadata to the KV cache synchronously.
marie: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? curious about ordering.
alex: here — pasted from nsys timeline (condensed):
```
[GPU] 0ms - launch GEMM fast path
[GPU] 2ms - GEMM fallback (soft) -> CPU memcpy
[CPU] 2.5ms - kvcache: persist slot_12 (sync)
[CPU] 3.5ms - batching thread waits on slot lock
[GPU] 5ms - next kernel queued
```
sam: that sync persist is bad — should be async flush or batched. explains latency jitter and perf regression in canary.
julie: we should add a test that injects fallback code-paths and measures tail latency under concurrent requests. also add a tracepoint when KV cache does sync persist.
marie: agree. For immediate profiling infra fix: create a qa/profile admission flow that allows pods annotated kubeprofile=true which our infra job admits and sets minimal extra caps and an init chown. keeps it off prod nodes and auditable.
alex: patch idea:
```
securityContext:
  runAsUser: 1000
  fsGroup: 1000
  capabilities:
    add: ["SYS_ADMIN","SYS_PTRACE"]
initContainers:
- name: chown-kv
  image: busybox
  command: ["sh","-c","chown -R 1000:1000 /var/lib/redwood/runtime/kv_cache"]
```
sam: add a note to eng-runtime runbook: "profiling mode" for capturing nsys/nvprof to avoid ad-hoc privileged pods.
julie: also file a follow-up with runtime team to make fallback persist asynchronous. ticket linked?
alex: opened INF-4217 with trace attached.
infra-bot: Deployment profile job created: profile-job-20260312-11. Check CI cluster namespace `perf-profiling` for pods.
marie: next steps: 1) qa/profile admission change (infra) 2) init-container chown approach (eng-runtime) 3) async persist work (runtime). I'll own #3 with alex.
alex: thanks everyone, I'll run the profile job and upload the full nsys timeline to the ticket.
sam: if anyone else runs into similar EACCES in perf tooling, ping me — we should standardize the docs on mounting hostPath for profiling.
